title: MIDO GDM: an innovative artificial intelligence-based prediction model for the development of gestational diabetes in Mexican women.
summary: In the described evaluation, the test-set AUC was 0.8471; an independent 50-person external set (27 GDM cases, 23 controls) produced AUC 0.9308, sensitivity 85.19% and specificity 86.96%. The external sample was confirmed separate from the development cohort, but it is small. The reported model-building description also has an unclear sample-count split; do not infer population-wide calibration or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: An artificial neural network uses nine clinical and demographic variables, selected with machine learning, to estimate GDM risk.
organization: University of Guadalajara, Health Sciences University Center, 44340, Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico

source_review.scope: The publisher full text describes a clinically specific Mexican gestational-diabetes risk result, with an artificial neural network using nine routinely collected variables and a separate 50-person external validation sample. The result-bearing version located is the publisher article dated 2023-04-28; exact-title/preprint searches found no earlier version. The active/archive catalogs have no same-result entry. The related genotype-informed GDM study uses a different SNP-plus-clinical model and reports distinct genetic findings, so it is related context rather than this model result. The external sample is small, and the paper does not establish improved maternal outcomes.
